evidence.supports: Official project page defines Belváros using nine named boundary streets. Geometry is a rough street-junction trace with documented connector/name gaps, not an exact published polygon.
The municipal handbook text independently lists the glassworks, Dr.László Elek, Tass street and Hajnal street estates. It supports identity; physical map outlines remain inferred.
Municipal planning notice distinguishes the former factory service housing from economic/factory areas. This reinforces preserving separate factory and housing names.
Independent index of OSM street records includes Hosszúgaz tanya, Szalmás tanya and Molnárkút street. The saved source ways preserve their actual name tags and shapes.
Official municipal planning/handbook index; useful contextual source, not asserted to publish the selected eight named boundaries.

Bodnár László study of Monostorpályi viticulture describes vineyard cultivation around Tejfeles after WWII. This supports a historical garden/field locality interpretation; it does not delimit the selected cell.
OSM-derived street guide corroborates the five short locality labels. Named farmyard sources independently preserve Csonkás tanya and Liliom tanya.
Official rural planning-map lead found through the municipal regulation; kept as a future refinement source. Not used to invent map boundaries in this batch.

Official structural-plan description names Cinevég and Keleti lakótelep. Physical estimates in this batch derive from saved OSM roads/landuse, rather than claiming these are extracted native planning polygons.
Local locality list corroborates Ráckert, Északi, Keleti, Cinevég and Fogarassy-tanya identity; exact extents are not stated.

geometryPolicy: No point buffers, circles, point-generated rectangles, Voronoi or convex hulls. Original map parcels/components are preserved when chosen; road cells and manual physical-map traces are explicitly estimated/lowConfidence.
